name: Current-location multi-cue orientation
summary: Provide coherent current destination context through page title, heading, navigational selection and programmatic state where needed.
problem: A user enters a nested view without knowing which page/section is current.
context: Multi-page websites/apps with repeated navigation and meaningful current destination.
observed_solution: Align descriptive page title/heading with correctly scoped current navigation item; use programmatic current state and distinguish named navigation landmarks as appropriate.
rationale: WCAG 2.4.2/2.4.6 mandate appropriate titles/headings (O02/O06); 2.4.8 adds a separate AAA location criterion (O07). WAI aria-current and nav labels O12/O14; GOV current-vs-active O18; USWDS current link O27; Primer O30/O31/O35/O37.
tradeoffs: Several signals can become redundant if all repeat the same information.
Breadcrumbs may be unnecessary on flat sites.
applicability: Nested page/section architecture with a current destination and repeated navigation.
non_applicability: Single self-explanatory document without repeated location choices.
Pure action toolbar with no navigational destination state.
accessibility_implications: Programmatic current state/landmark names aid orientation when used correctly; actual AT output untested.
responsive_implications: W04 recoverable routes and meaningful order apply when current nav is collapsed.
implementation_notes: Use context-correct current state, not just color.
SC 2.4.8 is AAA; do not mandate breadcrumbs or upgrade it to AA.

counterexamples.summary: A flat landing page with a clear title may not benefit from a redundant breadcrumb.

version_context: WCAG 2.2 2024; unpinned WAI/GOV/USWDS/Primer docs; primer/react pinned 7f5303d803986887187d86dcebaeda22a4dc6823
